why: The answer correctly states the truth-table rules for && and || but gives no explanation and does not work through the four combinations of p and q, so it states the rule without applying it.

concepts.quote: p && q is true only when both are true; p || q is false only when both are false.
concepts.why: These are the correct definitions of && and ||, given as rules without applying them value by value.
The answer says nothing about which operands get evaluated.
The answer makes no claim about the boolean type beyond using the words true and false.
